subject: Data Engineering
title: What Is Event-Driven Architecture?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is Event-Driven Architecture?.

hook.text: Instead of service A calling service B directly, A publishes an event. B reacts if it cares.

buildup.text: Event-driven architecture decouples services by having them communicate through published events.

discovery.text: Services become independent. Adding new reactions to an event requires no changes to the event producer.

twist.text: The downside: debugging is harder. When something goes wrong, there's no single call stack to trace.

climax.text: Event-driven systems are more flexible but demand strong observability to remain understandable.

punchline.text: Decouple the services. Invest in observability.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of event-driven architecture?
options: Services are decoupled and can evolve independently
